result.title: When Does Pre-Trained Capacity Help Causal Learning? From Scalar Prediction to Counterfactual Post-Training
result.comment: 10 pages. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop: Transitioning from Pre-Training to Post-Training
result.summary: How does pre-trained model capacity relate to performance after adaptation for causal tasks? We study two systems built on the Qwen 2.5 family: CausalLLM, which estimates scalar potential outcomes with treatment-specific heads, and CausalGen, which generates treatment-conditioned text or code using soft prefixes and factual supervised fine-tuning (SFT), counterfactual SFT, and preference alignment. Increasing backbone size from 0.5B to 1.5B yields mixed scalar-estimation results on IHDP, but improves CodeGen pass@1 from 0.267 to 0.575 and treatment-effect score from 0.231 to 0.515 after the complete generative pipeline. Within 0.5B CausalLLM, narrative inputs reduce mean sqrt(PEHE) from 1.842 to 1.780, a 3.4% improvement over tabular inputs; the 5.8% improvement over a no-LLM baseline combines changes in representation and input format. These descriptive comparisons motivate a distinction between available and convertible capacity. They do not isolate the contribution of post-training: the two systems differ in dataset, architecture, output modality, and supervision, and intermediate-stage evaluations are unavailable. With only two small backbones and three replications, the results support a hypothesis about capacity--adaptation alignment rather than a general scaling law or a demonstrated causal mechanism.

AI.brief_summary: 论文基于 Qwen 2.5 构建 CausalLLM（治疗特异输出头的标量潜在结果估计）与 CausalGen（soft prefix 条件生成，配合事实 SFT、反事实 SFT 与偏好对齐），比较 0.5B 与 1.5B 骨干在因果任务适配后的表现，并提出「可用容量」与「可转化容量」的区分假设。
AI.relevance_reason: 「可用容量 vs 可转化容量」的区分、soft prefix 条件状态与反事实 SFT 后的分阶段后训练，可提供核查线索：如何判断 latent 状态是否真正承载任务必要证据，以及监督如何把容量转化为可用推理状态；但该工作为纯文本因果任务、无视觉输入，联系较远，仅供参考。
